title: Pairing-induced Bloch oscillations in an interacting Kitaev chain
abstract: We study the peculiar dynamics of the Kitaev chain induced by nearest-neighbor (NN) interaction. We show that a strong NN interaction suppresses single-particle hopping but enhances pairing, resulting in a Wannier-Stark ladder. Based on the spin-fermion correspondence at the symmetry point, the model maps to a transverse field Ising model on a zigzag lattice, providing a clear physical picture and guiding experimental verification. The Wannier-Stark state corresponds to a localized domain wall between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases. It exhibits Bloch oscillation even in the absence of a longitudinal field, in contrast to previous works. Numerical simulations of time-dependent observables verify these conclusions. Our findings provide an example demonstrating emergent Stark many-body localization.
summary: This work investigates the complex dynamics of an interacting Kitaev chain subjected to nearest-neighbor interactions. The key finding is that these interactions induce Bloch oscillations via the formation of a Wannier-Stark ladder state, even without an external longitudinal field. This provides a concrete example of emergent many-body localization driven purely by internal quantum correlations.
main_problem: The study investigates the peculiar dynamics of the Kitaev chain when subjected to nearest-neighbor (NN) interactions, specifically focusing on the emergence of Bloch oscillations without an external longitudinal field.
main_result: Strong NN interaction enhances pairing and leads to a Wannier-Stark ladder state exhibiting Bloch oscillation intrinsically. This demonstrates emergent Stark many-body localization driven by internal interactions rather than disorder or applied fields.
method: The authors used diagonalization in the particle-number basis, derived an effective Hamiltonian ($H_{eff}$), and mapped the system to a transverse field Ising model on a zigzag lattice for analysis.
model_or_system: The primary system is the interacting spinless fermion Kitaev chain. It is mathematically related via spin-fermion correspondence to a transverse field Ising model defined on a zigzag lattice, which models domain wall dynamics between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases.
key_observables: Wannier-Stark ladder (WSL) formation, Bloch oscillation periodicity ($T_0 = \pi/\mu$), fidelity $F(t)$, average particle number $\langle n_j angle$, magnetization $m_j$, and bipartite Von Neumann entropy $S(t)$.
important_parameters: The nearest-neighbor interaction strength ($U$) relative to hopping ($	au$), pairing ($\Delta$), and chemical potential ($\mu$); the regime $|U| \gg |\mu|, |\Delta|, |	au|$ is crucial for deriving the effective Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The derivation of the effective Hamiltonian relies on the strong interaction limit ($|U| \gg |\mu|, |\Delta|, |	au|$). The mapping from spin operators to fermions is noted as not being a standard Jordan-Wigner transformation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level structures showing WSL formation, and show periodic revival of fidelity and domain wall oscillations in both the fermionic and spin representations, confirming periodicity $T_0 = \pi/\mu$.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the Kitaev chain dynamics under NN interaction to establish the WSL state. It then maps this system to a transverse field Ising model on a zigzag lattice using spin-fermion correspondence. Finally, it uses numerical simulations to confirm Bloch oscillations and emergent many-body localization in both representations.
why_interesting: The demonstration of intrinsic Bloch oscillations driven by pairing processes, rather than external fields or disorder, provides a clean theoretical platform for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated quantum materials relevant to AMO physics.
